title: THE SHAPE OF THE 41 — every op module exposes exactly one callable named `op`
measured: 41/41 modules define a public callable `op(...)` with a real typed signature (e.g. dct.op(signal,*,dct_type=2,axis=-1,D=8192); esprit.op(R,*,n_sources,D=8192)). Four modules define one extra helper: jpeg.dct_op, mlse.viterbi_op, polyphase.decompose, spectrogram.stft_op. So 45 entry points across 41 modules.
why_it_matters: The op NAME is carried by the MODULE, not the function. Any ToolEntry set is therefore keyed on the full dotted path srmech.signal_processing.closed_form_ops.<op>.op — 41 unique registry keys whose leaf is uniformly `op`.

title: closed_form_ops.__all__ EXISTS and lists 41 modules + PATH_A_OP_MODULES
measured: len(closed_form_ops.__all__) == 42; 41 entries are MODULES, 1 (PATH_A_OP_MODULES) is a tuple
consequence: The ratchet's documented exclusion #2 ('modules — a submodule bound into a package __all__ is a namespace re-export, not a callable') fires on all 41, and the non-callable exclusion fires on PATH_A_OP_MODULES. The package __all__ therefore contributes ZERO public surface points while looking fully declared.
severity: this is the mechanism, not the intent

title: ADJUDICATION OF §4(a): the absence is ACCIDENTAL, and the tree already contains the corrected predicate
question: Is closed_form_ops's absence from the ratchet's scan set deliberate or accidental?
measured: The scan DOES walk all 42 closed_form_ops modules (pkgutil.walk_packages, no _-prefixed component). The string 'closed_form_ops' appearing 0 times in the test file reflects a GENERIC walk, not an exclusion. The 41 op modules declare NO __all__. public_surface() reads `getattr(m,'__all__',()) or ()` with NO fallback, so a module with no __all__ contributes zero.
the_proof_it_is_accidental: tests/conftest.py:596 rosetta_live_objects() — walking the SAME package for the SAME purpose — does have the fallback: `names = getattr(mod,'__all__',None); if names is None: names = [n for n in dir(mod) if not n.startswith('_')]`. Two ratchets in the same tests/ directory disagree on scope by exactly this one clause. The Rosetta ledger consequently carries all 45 closed_form_ops entry points; the completeness ratchet carries zero.
verdict: ACCIDENTAL. There is no documented exclusion rule. The completeness ratchet's scope predicate is __all__-GATED, and __all__ is optional, so 'completeness' is completeness-relative-to-declared-exports, not completeness of the public surface. A module can leave the ratchet by declining to write __all__.

title: MCP tool list — same result

title: THE COUNTER-READING IS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT — dispatch reaches 8 of 41, not 41
brief_counter_reading: dispatch-by-string may be the deliberate calling convention, so 'not in __all__' may be correct-by-design
measured: registered_ops() at import returns 13 names: fft, ifft, rfft, sign_quantise, matched_filter, wiener, hdc_truncation, pi_cascade (the 8 dual-path ops) + form_function_rotate + 4 rbs_hdc_*. Calling dispatch(<name>) across the 41: 3 ran on a naive signal= kwarg, 5 more are KNOWN but raised TypeError on argument shape (so 8 known), and 33 raised UnknownOperationError.
registration_site: self-registration lives in srmech/signal_processing/path_b_ops/*.py (8 modules) — the dispatch table is populated BY PATH B, i.e. by the ops that HAVE two paths.
adjudication: dispatch is a PATH-ROUTER, not a name-resolver. It is CORRECTLY populated with exactly the ops that have a fork to route. Registering the 33 single-path ops in it would add a router for a fork that does not exist. So the README's usage block is NOT lying — it demonstrates the router. BUT the counter-reading does not rescue the surface, because (i) the correct calling convention for the other 33 is direct import of <module>.op, which appears nowhere in the README, and (ii) `dispatch` and `begin_cascade` are THEMSELVES unregistered, so a consumer with only introspect cannot find the router either.
verdict: COUNTER-READING REFUTED as a defence of the discovery gap; UPHELD as a defence of the dispatch table's contents.

title: README falsehood — settled, and it is narrower than 'the 41 are undocumented'
claim_checked: README line 253 makes the 41 headline feature #4 and names all 41; README line 272 shows dispatch("fft", path=PATH_A, signal=x) as the calling convention
measured: The README separately and correctly states at line 254 that 'Eight ops have full dual-path implementations'. Those 8 are EXACTLY the 8 dispatch-reachable ops. So the README is internally consistent on dispatch.
actual_gap: The README never states how to call the other 33. There is no example of `from srmech.signal_processing.closed_form_ops.wavelet import op`. A reader who follows only the shown convention gets UnknownOperationError on 33 of the 41 advertised ops.
verdict: NOT a doc falsehood about dispatch. IS a documentation gap about the direct-import convention, and a total discovery gap in introspect.

title: ADR-0009 / Rosetta — registering a Python op creates NO new C-peer obligation
the_decisive_fact: Of those 79, FORTY-TWO are already the closed_form_ops entry points (srmech.signal_processing.closed_form_ops.<op>.op), classified 12 c_dispatched / 29 composition_of_c / 1 non_compute. The C-parity obligation for the 41 ops is ALREADY ENUMERATED AND DISCHARGED-OR-TRACKED by the ledger.
the_rule: tests/conftest.py rosetta_live_objects() builds the ledger's denominator from the MODULE WALK over _ROSETTA_ROOTS (tests/rosetta_roots.py), NOT from the tool registry. Adding a ToolEntry adds no ledger row; removing one removes no ledger row. The two registries are independent by construction.
answer: NO new C-peer obligation. rc419 does NOT imply 41 new C peers. This is the single biggest de-risking finding for scope.

title: ALREADY_PUBLIC_ELSEWHERE — settled by identity AND value, not by name

verdict: CORRECTLY_PRIVATE (as tool rows), but ONE is a real carrier gap

RBSHDCInstrument is neither. That is a genuine, separate finding.

scope: the 6 REGISTRY_MUTATOR rows (register, clear_registry, lock_dispatch_table, unlock_dispatch_table, register_lazy_loader, clear_records)
verdict: CORRECTLY_PRIVATE — the stated reason HOLDS
reason_checked: The code's stated rationale is (i) registering the registrar inside the registry it mutates is circular, and (ii) 'these have no value contract — their whole effect is on state a later call observes.' Verified against the signatures: register(op_name,*,path,impl,...) -> None; clear_registry() -> None; lock/unlock_dispatch_table() -> None. All return None and mutate process-global state.
exit_condition_status: The code's own exit condition ('the registry gains a self-describing mutator row shape') has not been met.
verdict_detail: HOLDS. Do not register these. Note register_lazy_loader is in path_registry.__all__ but NOT in signal_processing.__all__ — the brief listed it among the 65; it is not one of them.

question: brief §4(b) — minimum correct fix, one shape recommended

candidates_evaluated.shape: register 41 ToolEntry rows keyed on the full dotted path
candidates_evaluated.why: the registry key srmech.signal_processing.closed_form_ops.wavelet.op is UNIQUE per op, resolves cleanly under registered_object_ids() (rpartition on '.' gives module=...wavelet, leaf=op), and puts each op in describe(), search() and the MCP list at op granularity. The PROTOCOL_UNIFORM objection ('seven rows called parse is not an answer a composer can act on') does NOT transfer: those 7 rows are INTERCHANGEABLE and the composer's real question is 'which adapter'; these 41 rows answer 41 DIFFERENT questions. The uniform leaf `op` is cosmetic — the key is the path.

candidates_evaluated.shape: one `dispatch` tool whose schema enumerates the 41 valid op names
candidates_evaluated.why: dispatch reaches 8 of 41 (F7). Enumerating 41 names in its schema would advertise 33 op names that raise UnknownOperationError. Populating the dispatch table for all 41 to make it true would add a path-router for ops that have exactly one path — wrong on its own terms.

candidates_evaluated.shape: add op names to the search index without registering
candidates_evaluated.why: violates ADR-0012 directly — search would return names describe() does not know and MCP cannot call, creating a second divergent index. The exact failure mode the introspect-is-the-contract stance exists to prevent.

candidates_evaluated.shape: extend describe() with a dispatch-table section
candidates_evaluated.why: does not make the 33 non-dispatchable ops callable or searchable at op granularity; it documents the router, which is the part that already works

recommended: register 38 closed_form_ops rows (41 minus the 3 ALREADY_PUBLIC_ELSEWHERE) + 23 signal_processing surface rows = 61 new ToolEntry rows; allowlist the 4 helpers + 8 path_b_ops as PROTOCOL_UNIFORM; fix the ratchet predicate.
